title: Titus Brandsma (1881–1942)
hook: a Dutch Carmelite who carried a letter from editor to editor, telling Catholic papers to refuse Nazi propaganda

segments.voice: Yesterday, Franz Jägerstätter, the farmer and sacristan who would not fight. Your line was one farmer said no. What small no did you say? Today, a priest who said no with a newspaper. Day nine hundred eleven.

A train compartment in the occupied Netherlands. A small, thin priest in a Carmelite habit, glasses, a briefcase on his knees. Inside the briefcase is a letter from the Dutch bishops. He gets off in one town, finds the office of the local Catholic newspaper, sits down with the editor, and explains the letter. Then back to the station, and the next town, and the next editor. He knows the occupiers will hear about this. Titus Brandsma, friar, professor and newspaperman, keeps going anyway.
screen: `A PRIEST WITH A BRIEFCASE.` → `EDITOR AFTER EDITOR.` → `HE KEEPS GOING.`

segments.voice: First, the professor. Titus was a Carmelite friar and a scholar of mysticism, a teacher at the Catholic university in Nijmegen. He also loved newspapers. He wrote for them, edited, and served as spiritual adviser to the Catholic journalists of his country. Second, the order. Under the occupation, the Nazi authorities demanded that Catholic papers print their propaganda, including notices for the Dutch Nazi party. The bishops said no: a Catholic paper that printed it could no longer call itself Catholic. Somebody had to carry that message to the editors, face to face, so no one could say they hadn't heard. Titus said he would go. Third, the cost. He was arrested and questioned. Asked why he resisted, he said, in substance, that the Nazi ideas could not be squared with the Gospel. He was sent from prison to prison, then to Dachau. Weak and sick, he was taken to the camp hospital and killed with an injection. Tradition says he gave his rosary to the nurse who did it. Fourth, the truth. Jesus says in John, in the Douay-Rheims: "And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." Set beside his life, it reads like a rule for newsrooms too: telling the truth includes refusing to print a lie, even a paid one.
screen: `A PROFESSOR WHO LOVED NEWSPAPERS.` · `NO NAZI PROPAGANDA IN OUR PAPERS.` · `ARRESTED, THEN DACHAU.` · `THE TRUTH SHALL MAKE YOU FREE.` · then, large: `KNOW THE TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: tell the truth in public. Settle, and breathe. Think of a place where you speak to more than one person: a team chat, a family thread, a meeting, a post. Is there something true that needs saying there, plainly and kindly? Or something false you've been letting pass, that you could quietly correct? Choose one sentence. Say it to yourself first, slowly, until it's clear and fair. If you pray, you can ask for Titus's steadiness. The bell holds the time.
Titus Brandsma. A Dutch Carmelite and journalist who carried the bishops' refusal of Nazi propaganda to editor after editor, and died at Dachau.
Your line: a journalist's courage. Today, say that one true sentence in public, or correct one thing that isn't true. Day nine hundred eleven.

howItsDone: Catholics honor St. Titus Brandsma as a martyr, and Catholic journalists' groups name him as a patron and example; Carmelites keep his feast.

what it means: a Carmelite journalist who was arrested for carrying the bishops' refusal of Nazi propaganda to editors.
what a scholar hears: a scholar of mysticism who treated a newspaper's refusal to print a lie as a matter of faith, and paid for it.

notes: Claims rule: no dates or counts of editors or towns; the title keeps the index years.
The bishops' position (Archbishop de Jong): Catholic papers must refuse NSB advertisements and propaganda, or lose their Catholic character. Confirm the paraphrase.
His answer under interrogation (the incompatibility of National Socialism with the Gospel) is paraphrased 'in substance', not quoted. Confirm.
Death at Dachau by lethal injection in the camp hospital; the rosary given to the nurse is kept as 'tradition says'. Confirm.
He also served as rector of the university at Nijmegen (left out). Confirm 'a teacher at the Catholic university'.
